dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies managing federal buildings, the Department of Energy, and green building certification entities.
dimensions.evidence: directs the Department of Energy to implement the standards as though such phase-out requirements had never taken effect

dimensions.assessment: Alters energy and building performance standards for new federal construction and major renovations by removing the 2030 fossil fuel phase-out mandate.
dimensions.evidence: The certification system and level may not prohibit a building from obtaining a certification... solely based on direct or indirect consumption of fossil fuels.

dimensions.assessment: Changes regulatory requirements for federal building construction and energy use, but specifies no direct budgetary appropriations or revenue impacts.
Repeals specific Code of Federal Regulations subparts, amends the Energy Conservation and Production Act, and requires the Department of Energy to issue revised regulations.
dimensions.evidence: Subpart B of part 435, and subpart B of part 433, of title 10, Code of Federal Regulations... shall have no force or effect.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change to federal building energy standards and certification rules.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Energy shall issue such new or revised regulations

missing_information: Long-term energy cost savings or expenses resulting from repealing the fossil fuel phase-out standards.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill repeals certain federal building energy efficiency performance standards that phase out fossil fuel use by 2030, sets transition rules, and adjusts green building certification rules regarding fossil fuel consumption.

related.label: H.Res. 1189
related.title: Providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 4690) to amend the Energy Conservation and Production Act to repeal certain Federal building energy efficiency performance standards, and for other purposes; providing for consideration of the resolution (H. Res. 1182) expressing support for rural communities across the United States as stewards of the environment, major suppliers of United States energy resources, critical providers of food production and manufacturing capacity, and drivers of national economic stability, and recognizing the work of the House of Representatives in the 119th Congress in support of those vital communities; providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 1897) to amend the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to optimize conservation through resource prioritization, incentivize wildlife conservation on private lands, provide for greater incentives to recover listed species, create greater transparency and accountability in recovering listed species, streamline the permitting process, eliminate barriers to conservation, and restore congressional intent; and providing for consideration of the bill (H.R. 5587) to amend the Geothermal Steam Act of 1970 to waive the requirement for a Federal drilling permit for certain activities, to exempt certain activities from the requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, and for other purposes.
